The handoff, recall, thread tools, resume and `cedia threads` are all in place. The final `bun test` ran after the last edit: 214 pass, 5 skip, 0 fail. `bun run typecheck` is clean. `test/threads.test.ts` (17 tests) and `test/layers.test.ts` pass, and I did not edit the test files.

What changed, following the handoff plan:

- **`src/clients/headless/main.ts`**: the writer now either resumes the thread's last session (same model) or starts a new one. Its preamble carries the resume context for a new session of an existing thread. A session that returns `handoff` writes its note to the thread, prints a stderr line, and continues in a new session on the same model with `<handoff>` in the preamble. The fallback and fix calls go through the same handoff loop. The result gets `thread` and `sessions`, and a `state` event is appended. Text output also prints `cedia thread: <id>` to stderr.
- **`src/cli.ts`**: `--thread`, `--handoff-at` (rejects values below 1000 with exit 2), the `threads` subcommand, and usage lines.
- **`src/clients/headless/threads-cmd.ts`** (new): `cedia threads`, `threads show <id>`, `threads send <id> <text…>`. Usage errors return 2 and other errors return 1.
- **`SPEC.md`**: a new "Threads, handoff, recall" section, and `handoff` added to the TurnEnd reason and result subtype in Core shapes.

Earlier-session pieces (`threads.ts`, `handoff.ts`, `tools/threads.ts`, the loop changes in `run.ts`, and the types) were checked, not rewritten.

Open points:
- The baseline had one failing test file and one error, which are now fixed.
- Everything was tested with the faux provider only. No real model was run, so the handoff trigger and the note quality have not been seen against a live provider.
- I did not add a `cedia thread:` stderr-format test; no existing test asserts the exact stderr text.
